## Build, test, and lint commands

- `npm run dev` (runs `predev` first, which executes `node scripts/prepare-legacy.mjs`)
- `npm run build` (runs `prebuild` first, which executes `node scripts/prepare-legacy.mjs`)
- `npm run start`
- `npm run lint` (uses `next lint`; this repo can prompt for ESLint setup if config is not initialized)

- Targeted tests:
  - `npm run test:price` (runs `scripts/test-price-snapshot-utils.mjs`)
  - `node --test tests/player-skill-stats-utils.test.mjs`
  - Single test by name: `node --test tests/player-skill-stats-utils.test.mjs --test-name-pattern "resolvePlayerDetailApiRequest"`
- There is no repo-wide `npm test` script.

- Operational commands used in normal workflows:
  - `npm run generate:top-players` (refreshes `src/data/top-players.json`)
  - `npm run rollout:status` (prints active prerender tier and effective limits)
  - `npm run revalidate:call -- --endpoint <url> --secret <secret> --paths /players,/market --player-ids <id1,id2>`
  - `npm run db:migrate:blog`, `npm run db:seed:blog-users` (blog CMS setup)

## High-level architecture

- This is a Next.js App Router app with route surfaces for `/`, `/players`, `/player/[slug]`, `/tools`, `/market`, `/blogs`, and API handlers under `app/api/*`.
- Shared page chrome is centralized in `app/components/SiteChrome.js` (desktop nav, mobile nav, footer). Most top-level pages render inside it.

- Player data + SEO pipeline is shared across pages:
  - `src/data/top-players.json` is the canonical player ID list (generated by `scripts/generate-top-players.mjs`).
  - `src/lib/server/top-players.mjs` fetches player batches/filter metadata and applies in-memory caching.
  - `src/lib/server/player-seo-contract.mjs` normalizes mixed API payloads, builds metadata/JSON-LD/attribute sections, and resolves slug-to-player IDs.
  - `app/page.js`, `app/players/page.js`, `app/market/page.js`, `app/tools/page.js`, and `app/player/[slug]/page.js` reuse that server pipeline.

- Price data is client-refreshed through Next API routes:
  - `/api/player-price` and `/api/player-price-history` query Supabase `price_snapshots` and use rank/timeout fallback logic (`src/lib/server/price-snapshot-utils.mjs`).

- Tools/watchlist routing model:
  - `/tools` is the hub.
  - `/watchlist` permanently redirects to `/tools?tool=watchlist`.
  - Compatibility routes `/squad-builder`, `/compare`, `/shard-calculator` redirect into `/tools`.

- Legacy compatibility flow:
  - `scripts/prepare-legacy.mjs` copies `assets/` to `public/assets/`, extracts legacy body HTML, and generates `public/assets/js/legacy-app.bundle.mjs`.
  - `/legacy` renders the generated legacy shell (`app/legacy/page.js` + `app/legacy-app-shell.js`).

- Blog subsystem:
  - Public blog pages use server-side loaders in `src/lib/server/blog/public.mjs` and SEO helpers in `src/lib/server/blog/seo.mjs`.
  - Blog revalidation is centralized in `src/lib/server/blog/revalidation.mjs` and invoked by `/api/revalidate`.

## Key conventions

- Preserve legacy DOM contracts in `src/lib/legacy-parity-contract.mjs` (required IDs/classes/selectors and nav attributes are relied on across pages and interactions).
- Do not hand-edit generated artifacts:
  - `src/lib/legacy-body.html`
  - `public/assets/js/legacy-app.bundle.mjs`

- Keep navigation links compatible with existing interception logic by preserving both `href` and `data-link` / `data-nav-link` attributes in shared nav/footer markup.

- Reuse canonical normalization helpers instead of ad-hoc parsing:
  - Search text: `app/components/search-normalization.js`
  - Mixed player payload normalization: `normalizePlayerStableRecord` / `preferPlayerStableRecord`
  - Legacy ID handling: `normalizeLegacyPlayerId`

- Watchlist identity is composite and must stay consistent across players, player detail, and watchlist flows:
  - `getPlayerUniqueId` format: `${playerId}_${rank}_${untradable}`
  - Shared storage/event coupling: `watchlist`, `watchlistPlayers`, `toolsSquadState`, `toolsSupplementalPlayers`, `selectedFieldTheme`, `squad_builder_roundtrip_state`, and the `watchlist-updated` window event.

- For player skill/training payloads used in client tools, route through local API proxies (`/api/players/[playerId]`, `/api/skill-boosts/[skillId]`, `/api/training/boosts`) via `app/components/player-skill-stats-utils.js` rather than calling external endpoints directly.

- Keep tool query behavior aligned with `ToolsInteractions` normalization:
  - Supported tool states are `squadbuilder`, `compare`, and `watchlist`.
  - Alias handling currently maps `squad-builder` -> `squadbuilder`.
